name: Gabapentin
toxicities: Label-reported effects include somnolence, dizziness, ataxia, fatigue, and altered mental status.

Serious risks include potentially fatal respiratory depression, including in overdose alone or with CNS depressants; DRESS, anaphylaxis/angioedema, and suicidal thoughts or behavior have also been reported.
Abrupt discontinuation can increase seizure frequency; rare withdrawal symptoms have been reported after stopping higher-than-recommended use.
summary: An analogue of GABA also known as Neurontin, originally developed to treat epilepsy. Commonly prescribed for neuropathic pain, it also has pronounced anxiolytic effects leading to its use in treating anxiety disorders.
metabolism: Does not undergo appreciable metabolism in humans. It is eliminated by the kidneys as unchanged gabapentin; hepatic CYP metabolism is not a major clearance pathway.
generalRisks: The DailyMed label associates gabapentin with serious, life-threatening, or fatal respiratory depression when combined with CNS depressants, including opioids, or in people with respiratory impairment. It also warns about sedation/dizziness and impaired driving, DRESS, anaphylaxis/angioedema, suicidal thoughts or behavior, and increased seizure frequency after abrupt discontinuation.
saferUse: Avoid driving or operating complex machinery until the effect on alertness and coordination is known.
Use caution with opioids or other CNS depressants and respiratory impairment; the label advises monitoring for sedation and respiratory depression.

Do not stop abruptly; discuss gradual discontinuation with the prescriber. Seek immediate care for breathing difficulty or swelling of the lips, tongue, throat, or face, and promptly report fever/rash or emerging suicidal thoughts.
